desc:
A brand voice guide for consistent copy describes how your business sounds, in words that anyone can follow. Ecom Swift LLC studies your real writing, agrees the tone with you and delivers a guide your team, freelancers and writing tools can use.

## What is a brand voice guide?

A brand voice guide is a short document that explains how your business speaks. It describes your tone in everyday words, lists the phrases you use and avoid, and shows examples of good and weak copy side by side. Anyone who writes for you can read it in a few minutes and match the style.

It is different from a logo or color guide. Those control how the brand looks, while the voice guide controls how it reads.

## Why a consistent voice matters

When several people write for one brand, the voice drifts. The website sounds formal, the emails sound casual, and the social posts sound like a third person wrote them. Customers may not name the problem, but they notice that the business feels uncertain about who it is.

A consistent voice builds recognition and trust over time. It also saves effort, because an editor can point to a rule instead of arguing about taste. For leads and sales, the effect is indirect: a clear voice makes your offers easier to read and your promises easier to believe. Results still depend on the offer and the audience, but a steady voice removes one avoidable source of friction.

## What a strong voice guide contains

- A plain description of your tone, such as warm, direct and practical, with a sentence explaining each word.
- Words and phrases to use, taken from your best existing copy.
- Words and phrases to avoid, including jargon, filler and anything that sounds like someone else.
- Before and after examples drawn from your own texts.
- Rules for sentence length, punctuation, capitalization and how you address the reader.
- Notes for each channel, such as your website, email and social posts.
- Guidance on humor, urgency and how to handle complaints or bad news.
- A short briefing sheet that can be pasted into AI writing tools to steer their output.
- A checklist an editor can run through before anything is published.
- A section on what never changes, even when the format does.

## How we create the guide

We start by collecting samples: pages from your website, recent emails, posts and any older material you like. We read them for patterns in word choice, rhythm and attitude. Then we talk through how you want to sound, because the best existing copy and the voice you want are not always the same.

We draft the guide and test it by rewriting a few of your real texts with it, so you can see the rules working. The Basic package gives you a compact guide with tone and word lists. Standard adds more examples, channel notes, the briefing sheet for writing tools and a round of changes. Premium adds a larger study, a test rewrite of several real texts, reusable templates, an editor's checklist and a team briefing.

## Do and avoid

**Do:**
- Describe your voice with real examples, not only adjectives.
- Keep the guide short enough that people will open it.
- Use it as the first brief for every new writer or tool.
- Update it when your audience or product changes.
- Ask a new writer to try it and report what was unclear.

**Avoid:**
- Choosing words like innovative or passionate that every company claims.
- Writing rules so strict that no one can follow them.
- Copying the voice of a larger competitor.
- Treating the guide as finished forever.
- Changing the voice for each platform until the brand feels like several businesses.

## Who a voice guide helps

This service suits an owner who has started to hire freelancers and wants new writers to sound like the brand from the first draft. It suits a growing store whose product pages, emails and social posts were written at different times by different people. It also suits a team that has started using AI writing tools and wants the output to match the brand, not a generic style.

## What we need from you

Send links or files for up to a handful of pieces you consider typical, plus any copy you dislike so we know what to avoid. Tell us who your customers are and how you want them to feel. A short call or a written answer to a few questions is enough. We never ask for passwords, because everything we need is public copy or files you choose to share.
